question: In March 2025, the 7th meeting of the National Board for Wildlife held at _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gir National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **7th meeting of the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL)** was held at the **Gir National Park**, which is one of the most prominent wildlife sanctuaries in India.
 
• **Gir National Park** is located in the state of **Gujarat** and is famously known as the last abode of the **Asiatic Lions**.
 
• The National Board for Wildlife (NBWL) is a statutory organization under the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**, and serves as an apex body for reviewing and approving wildlife-related projects and policies in India.
 
• The board consists of experts, government officials, and stakeholders to ensure the conservation of wildlife and its habitats.
 
• Gir National Park is known for its significant contributions to the **conservation of endangered species** and promoting wildlife tourism in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gir National Park**:

 
 
• **Location:** Situated in **Junagadh district, Gujarat**, Gir National Park is spread over approximately 1,412 sq. km.
 
• **Flora and Fauna:** The park is home to a variety of flora and fauna, including the **Asiatic Lion**, leopards, antelopes, and crocodiles, along with over 400 species of plants.
 
• **Tourism:** Gir attracts numerous tourists every year, contributing to the state’s economy while raising awareness about wildlife conservation.
 
• **Conservation Efforts:** The park has achieved great success in increasing the population of Asiatic Lions through dedicated conservation programs.
 
• The **Asiatic Lion Census 2020** reported approximately **674 lions**, marking a significant increase in their population.
 
 
 
• **National Board for Wildlife (NBWL):**
 
 
• The NBWL is chaired by the **Prime Minister of India** and serves as the apex body for wildlife conservation in the country.
 
• It is tasked with **approving projects** that affect protected areas and ensuring the sustainable development of wildlife habitats.
 
• It also advises the central government on matters related to the protection of wildlife under the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**.
 
 
 
• **Other National Parks Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Manas National Park:** Located in Assam, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its biodiversity, including tigers, elephants, and golden langurs.
 
• **Kanha National Park:** Situated in Madhya Pradesh, it is famous for its tiger reserves and the reintroduction of the barasingha (swamp deer).
 
• **Silent Valley National Park:** Located in Kerala, it is known for its tropical rainforests and is home to the endangered lion-tailed macaque.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972:** This act provides the framework for the protection of endangered species and the regulation of wildlife sanctuaries and national parks in India.
 
• **Conservation Programs:** Several initiatives, such as **Project Tiger** and **Project Lion**, are dedicated to conserving India’s iconic wildlife species.
 
• **Asiatic Lions:** Unlike African lions, Asiatic lions are smaller and have a distinct fold of skin along their bellies. They are exclusively found in Gir National Park.
 
• **Environmental Significance:** National parks like Gir play a crucial role in maintaining ecological balance and promoting biodiversity in India.
